sheet-27-1.description: The main part of sheet 27 covers the southern edge of central East Rutherford and the adjoining blocks of Carlstadt at 100 feet to an inch. Paterson Avenue crosses it on a long diagonal from Hackensack Street at the upper left to Hoboken Road; Hoboken Road runs down the right-centre of the sheet carrying the dash-dot East Rutherford / Carlstadt borough line, and south of William Street the same road is lettered Paterson Avenue. West of Hoboken Road lie Prospect Terrace, Hackensack, Cornelia, Vreeland Avenue, Jane, Enoch and William Streets, with Garden Street at the top. East of the road the Carlstadt blocks run from Sixth to Fourteenth Street (marked not opened) as far as Broad on the right edge, with the tracks of the N. J. & N. Y. Railroad crossing at Twelfth Street beside the Erie R.R. station and a freight house. Housing is mostly frame dwellings. Institutions are St. Joseph's R.C. Church and parochial school on Hackensack Street, and the Lincoln School of fire-proof concrete construction, built 1917, on Vreeland Avenue. Industry clusters along Paterson Avenue and the railroad: The Rutherford Co., makers of ladies' garments; an automobile repair garage at Cornelia; the Neuweller embroidery works; the Sussex Rubber Co., makers of rubber tubes and heels; S. Klaber & Co. marble works with planing and cutting rooms at Ninth Street; the Interborough Coal Co.; G. Depken & Sons' coal yard; and K. Hasselhuhn & Son, coal and wood, with ground marked vacant beyond. The blocks south of Twelfth Street in Carlstadt are drawn with dashed outlines as undeveloped. A heavy line in the lower left cuts off part 2 and a blank area belonging to sheet 23.
notes: Enoch Street is lettered Enogh on the sheet.
Lincoln School, fire-proof concrete construction, built 1917, on Vreeland Avenue.
Erie R.R. station and freight house where the N. J. & N. Y. Railroad crosses Paterson Avenue (Hoboken Road) at Twelfth Street.

The Paterson Avenue / Prospect Terrace and Enoch Street / Paterson Avenue junctions were excluded: the first paired a lot line at the sheet corner (4.6 m), the second has two modern nodes about 30 m apart.

Scale 100 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy line. Part 1 (main): East Rutherford along Paterson Avenue (diagonal) from Prospect Terrace and Hackensack to Enoch and William, Hoboken Road (Paterson Av south of William) as the Carlstadt borough line, and Carlstadt from 6th to 14th Street east to Broad; Erie R.R. station and coal yards at the bottom. Part 2 (lower left): northern East Rutherford at the Wallington line, about 2.5 km north-west: Carlton Av, Union, York, Jersey, Locust Av, Hope, Grant, Elm, New, Paterson Av (William St on the Wallington side); drawn at its own rotation (about 35 deg against 52 deg). Upper left of the heavy line near the '23' label is left blank (sheet 23).

sheet-27-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 27, cut off from the main map by a heavy line in the lower left, shows the northern corner of East Rutherford at the Wallington line, about two and a half kilometres north-west of the rest of the sheet, at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 18 degrees against the main part, with its own north arrow. Paterson Avenue runs down the right side along the heavy line, carrying the dash-dot East Rutherford / Wallington borough line, with William Street lettered on the Wallington side. Carlton Avenue runs down the left edge and curves north-east at the top towards Jersey Street. Between them Union and York Streets run north from Locust Avenue, and Locust Avenue, Hope, Grant, Elm and New Streets cross the part. The blocks (numbered 4, 5 and 9 to 15) are laid out in narrow building lots, but most are empty: a few frame dwellings and flats stand near Paterson Avenue and at the lower end of Carlton Avenue, with a grocery on Paterson Avenue at Locust and a Methodist Episcopal church at Carlton Avenue and Hope Street. The upper corner of the part, around the large figure 23, is left blank because sheet 23 draws it, and the label E. Rutherford is printed across it. The scale bar and copyright line of the sheet run along the bottom edge below New Street.
notes: This part lies about 2.5 km north-west of part 1 (Paterson Avenue at Hope Street, at the Wallington line) and is drawn at its own rotation.
Methodist Episcopal church at Carlton Avenue and Hope Street.

Scale 100 ft. Two parts divided by a heavy line. Part 1 (main): East Rutherford along Paterson Avenue (diagonal) from Prospect Terrace and Hackensack to Enoch and William, Hoboken Road (Paterson Av south of William) as the Carlstadt borough line, and Carlstadt from 6th to 14th Street east to Broad; Erie R.R. station and coal yards at the bottom. Part 2 (lower left): northern East Rutherford at the Wallington line, about 2.5 km north-west: Carlton Av, Union, York, Jersey, Locust Av, Hope, Grant, Elm, New, Paterson Av (William St on the Wallington side); drawn at its own rotation (about 35 deg against 52 deg). Upper left of the heavy line near the '23' label is left blank (sheet 23).

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 shows the northern end of the East Rutherford / Carlstadt border at 50 feet to an inch. A single road runs down the middle of the sheet carrying the dash-dot borough line: it is lettered Paterson Avenue north of Garden Street and Hoboken Road south of it, with East Rutherford to the west and Carlstadt to the east. On the East Rutherford side Maple, Poplar and Herman Streets run in from the left edge, the Erie Railroad crosses the upper left corner on a long diagonal, and a second, diagonal Paterson Avenue comes up from the lower left to meet the road near Garden Street, with Mozart Street along the bottom and Laurel Place leaving it. On the Carlstadt side Garden, Lincoln and Union Streets run east to Broad Street on the right edge, where the end of Orchard Street is lettered in the margin. The ground is thinly built. The largest works are the C. R. Soley Co., makers of mouldings and trim, with a planing mill and sash factory and lumber sheds between the railroad and Poplar Street, and the Scharg Bros. silk mill with its repair shop, pump house and coal house between Garden and Lincoln Streets. The Public Service Corporation of N.J. car barn, used for storage only, with a caretaker's dwelling, stands in a large lot north of Garden Street. Smaller premises are a garage with a gasoline tank and a lunch wagon at the fork of Paterson Avenue, a saloon and hitching shed opposite, John Caneyari's plating shop, and the pearl button factory of Wm. Bradac, marked closed, on Lincoln Street at Broad. The rest are frame dwellings and stores.
notes: The Erie Railroad (lettered E. R. R.) crosses the upper left; its crossing of Paterson Avenue, matched to the modern Bergen County Line, was rejected at 4.1 m.
Public Service Corporation of N.J. car barn, capacity 16 cars, in use for storage only.
Scharg Bros. silk mill (winding and weaving) between Garden and Lincoln Streets; C. R. Soley Co. sash factory and planing mill on Poplar Street.
Wm. Bradac pearl button factory on Lincoln Street at Broad, marked closed.

Scale 50 ft. One part. Paterson Av (vertical, north of Garden) and Hoboken Road (south of Garden) as the East Rutherford / Carlstadt borough line; west side: Maple, Poplar, Herman, Mozart, diagonal Paterson Av, Laurel Pl, Erie R.R. across the top left; east side: Garden, Lincoln, Union to Broad (right edge). Public Service car barn, Scharg Bros. silk mill, C. R. Soley Co. sash factory.

sheet-49.description: Sheet 49 covers the centre of East Rutherford and the adjoining north-western corner of Carlstadt at 100 feet to an inch. Hoboken Road runs down the sheet a little right of centre and carries the dash-dot East Rutherford / Carlstadt borough line; Mozart Street (Union on the Carlstadt side) crosses the top and Prospect Terrace the bottom. West of Hoboken Road the East Rutherford blocks lie between Grove Street on the left edge and the road, cut diagonally by Paterson Avenue, with Clinton Place, Humboldt, Uhland, Everett Place, Washington Place, Lincoln Place, Boiling Springs Avenue and High crossing, and Randolph Avenue, Laurel Place, Garden and George running north-south. East of the road the Carlstadt blocks run from Union to Second Street between Hoboken Road and Broad on the right edge, with Washington, Jefferson, Madison, Monroe and First between. The area is mostly frame dwellings with stores and shops along Paterson Avenue and near Hoboken Road. Public buildings are the Municipal Square School, Borough Hall with the fire department on Everett Place, a small triangular park at Park Avenue, and the Immanuel Lutheran Church and rectory on Washington Place. Trades include Claus Ahrens, contractor, with his lumber sheds and yard between Paterson and Randolph Avenues, a celluloid comb and metal novelty works near High Street, and on the Carlstadt side Concordia Hall, Turn Hall, the J. M. Woodward winding and warping shop, Julius Koch's carpenter shop and the Geist Hat & Cap Co. at First and Broad. The south-east corner below Second Street is left blank as part of sheet 51; the margins name sheets 35, 36, 40, 44, 50 and 27.
notes: Garfield, N.J. is printed above the sheet number: the sheet belongs to the Garfield volume of the 1917 atlas.
Claus Ahrens, contractor, with lumber sheds and a scattered lumber yard between Paterson Avenue and Randolph Avenue.
Geist Hat & Cap Co., makers of men's and ladies' hats, at First Street and Broad, Carlstadt.

Scale 100 ft. One part. Central East Rutherford: Mozart to Prospect Ter between Grove and Hoboken Road (Paterson Av diagonal; Randolph Av, Laurel Pl, Windsor Av, Washington Pl, Lincoln Pl, Boiling Springs Av, Garden, George, High), and Carlstadt east of Hoboken Road from Union to 2nd St, to Broad at the right edge. Borough Hall, Municipal Square School, Concordia Hall, Turn Hall.

sheet-50.description: Sheet 50 covers the northern part of Carlstadt at 100 feet to an inch, from Garden Street at the top down to Second Street, between Broad Street on the left edge and Passaic Avenue on the right edge, where the dash-dot Carlstadt / Woodridge borough line runs and the ends of Madison, James, Rose and Charter Oak Streets in Woodridge are lettered in the margin. Division Avenue, Central Avenue and Summit Avenue run up the sheet; Orchard, Lincoln, Union, Washington, Jefferson, Madison, Monroe and First Streets cross it, and Interstate Place is a short street off Central Avenue. Above Garden Street only house fronts are drawn. The upper right quarter, east of Central Avenue and north of Washington Street, is the open ground of Bobbink & Atkins, nurserymen, with a large compass rose. Elsewhere the blocks are filled with frame dwellings, more closely built towards Broad Street. Industry includes the Franco-American Chemical Works, makers of pharmaceutical supplies, at Garden and Broad; the Smith & Nichols paraffin, wax and candle factory on Garden at Division Avenue; the E. Kramer Machine Co. and the Standard Brass Works on Madison Street; Emil Hensle's machine and tool works on Monroe; Rutch & Son's embroidery works; and A. Haessig's hand embroidery works near Second Street and Summit Avenue. The Hackensack Water Co. has two reservoirs, one covered, at Summit Avenue and Madison. Mt. Pleasant Park with a dance hall and bowling alley fills a block on Jefferson at Division Avenue, there is a second dance hall on Monroe at Broad, the Carlstadt Baptist Church stands on Madison at Broad, and Hose Co. No. 2 is on Division Avenue at Jefferson.
notes: Passaic Avenue on the Woodridge line is today Fritsch Avenue; its junctions on this sheet were placed 10 to 13 m off by the detector and rejected.
Bobbink & Atkins, nurserymen, occupy the open ground east of Central Avenue and north of Washington Street.
Hackensack Water Co. reservoirs of 507,000 and 1,380,000 gallons at Summit Avenue and Madison Street.

Scale 100 ft. One part. Carlstadt north of 2nd St: Garden to 2nd between Broad (left edge) and Passaic Av (right edge; today Fritsch Avenue, the Wood-Ridge line), with Division Av, Central Av, Summit Av, Orchard, Lincoln, Interstate Pl. Franco-American Chemical Works, Smith & Nichols paraffin factory, E. Kramer Machine Co., Hackensack Water Co. reservoirs, Mt. Pleasant Park, Bobbink & Atkins nursery.

sheet-51.description: Sheet 51 shows the business centre of Carlstadt at 50 feet to an inch, between Hoboken Road on the left edge, where the dash-dot line of the Borough of East Rutherford runs, and the blocks east of Broad Street on the right. Second, Third and Fourth Streets cross the upper half; Small Street runs from Fourth down to Hackensack Street, which crosses the lower half on a slant and widens into a small open place at Broad, marked by a dashed half circle. Fifth Street (Lilac Lane) runs below it from Hoboken Road to Broad, and Sixth Street lies along the bottom; east of Broad, Fifth Street is drawn separately. The blocks hold frame dwellings, flats and tenements, with a dense row of shops along Hackensack Street and Broad: saloons, groceries, bakeries, a bank, an insurance office, a barber, a cigar store, a drug store, a meat market, a hardware store, a jeweller, a cobbler and a moving picture house. Public buildings are Carlstadt Public School No. 1 with the borough hall, fire house and bell tower beside it on Third Street, and the post office on Broad. Larger premises include Wm. Umbach's bottling works and a hand printing shop on Second Street, a pool room, bar and bowling alley at Second and Broad, the greenhouses of Jacob H. Ullmann, florist, between Third and Fourth (some marked to be removed), G. Zimmermann's hotel and hall with stage, dining room and bowling alleys at Hackensack and Broad, and a hay and feed storehouse near Sixth Street. Retaining walls cross block 69. The top and bottom margins outline sheets 49, 50, 27 and 53.
notes: Fifth Street west of Broad is also lettered Lilac Lane, the name it carries today; the modern Lilac Lane meets Broad at the Sixth Street node.
Carlstadt Public School No. 1 with the borough hall and fire house on Third Street.
G. Zimmermann's hotel, hall and bowling alleys at Hackensack Street and Broad; Jacob H. Ullmann's greenhouses between Third and Fourth.

Scale 50 ft. One part. Carlstadt centre between Hoboken Road (left edge, borough line) and Broad, 2nd to 6th St, with Small St and Hackensack St; 5th St (Lilac Lane) at the bottom left. Carlstadt Public School No. 1 and Borough Hall, post office, J. H. Ullmann greenhouses, G. Zimmermann hall.

sheet-52.description: Sheet 52 covers a residential part of Carlstadt east of Broad Street at 50 feet to an inch, from Second Street at the top to Sixth Street at the bottom. Division Avenue runs down the left third of the sheet, Central Avenue down the middle as far as Hackensack Street, Berry Avenue from Hackensack Street southwards (marked not opened between Fifth and Sixth Streets) and Summit Avenue along the right edge. Third Street crosses the whole sheet, Fourth Street only the strip west of Division Avenue, and Hackensack Street runs across the middle on a slant. The left margin repeats the eastern half of the blocks on sheet 51, with a bottling works, saloon, grocery and offices facing Broad. The blocks are mostly large lots with scattered frame dwellings and outbuildings; the two blocks between Fifth and Sixth Streets are laid out in lots with only one house. The notable premises are on the block bounded by Second, Third, Division and Central: the 1st German Evangelical Church, stuccoed, with its two-storey Sunday school, and the underwear factory of Theo. Goers, manufacturer of ladies' undergarments, powered by a gasoline engine. A small concrete-block dwelling stands on Central Avenue near Hackensack Street. Division Avenue is drawn 31 ft wide south of Hackensack Street, where it is lettered Division St at the bottom, and 50 ft wide above it. A compass rose sits in block 64. The margins name sheets 50, 51, 53 and 55.
notes: Fifth Street between Division Avenue and Berry Avenue and Central Avenue south of Hackensack Street no longer exist; Park Lane now runs diagonally across this ground.
Theo. Goers, manufacturer of ladies' undergarments, and the 1st German Evangelical Church with its Sunday school, between Second and Third Streets.

Scale 50 ft. One part. Carlstadt from 2nd to 6th St between the left margin (Broad side blocks of sheet 51) and Summit Av (right edge): Division Av, Central Av, Berry Av, Hackensack St. 1st German Evangelical Church, Theo. Goers underwear factory. 5th St between Division and Berry and Central Av south of Hackensack no longer exist.

sheet-53-1.description: The main part of sheet 53 covers southern Carlstadt at 100 feet to an inch, from Sixth Street at the top to Sixteenth Street at the bottom, between Broad Street along the left edge and Passaic Avenue on the right. Division Avenue and Berry Avenue run down the sheet between them as far as Eleventh Street; Seventh to Eleventh Streets cross the upper half, and below the N. J. & N. Y. Railroad, which crosses at Twelfth Street, Thirteenth to Sixteenth Streets continue only between Broad and the line of Division Avenue. Fourteenth Street is marked not opened, and the blocks south of it (120, 125, 130) are drawn with dashed outlines as platted but undeveloped land. The built-up blocks near Broad hold frame dwellings and stores, with the Meyer & Co. embroidery shop and Mueller's Casino at Seventh Street, greenhouses on Sixth, a stone cutting yard, and Lincoln Public School No. 3 on Sixth Street between Division and Berry Avenues. The Carlstadt Cemetery and the Berry Lawn Cemetery fill the blocks between Seventh and Eighth Streets. East of Berry Avenue the blocks to Passaic Avenue are laid out in lots but almost empty, with Voh's Ice Co. ice house beyond Tenth Street. Along the railroad stand the Carlstadt Consumers Ice Co. plant with a 50-ton ice machine at Eleventh Street and Division Avenue, the ruins of a fire on Broad, and A. Gerke's machine shop and an old and vacant building on Thirteenth Street. The lower right quarter is a separate inset (part 2) of the Gregg Co. works in Lodi, cut off by a heavy line.
notes: The N. J. & N. Y. Railroad (today's Pascack Valley Line) crosses at Twelfth Street; its crossing of Broad Street was used as a control point (modern way: PB Connection Track).
Fourteenth Street is marked not opened; the blocks south of it are drawn with dashed outlines.
Thirteenth Street is drawn about 20 ft wide and Division Avenue about 31 ft wide at their junction.
Eleventh Street no longer exists between Broad and Division Avenue.

Scale 100 ft. Two parts. Part 1 (main): southern Carlstadt from 6th to 16th St between Broad (left edge) and Passaic Av, with Division Av and Berry Av; N.J. & N.Y. R.R. crossing at 12th St; Berry Lawn and Carlstadt cemeteries, Lincoln Public School No. 3, Carlstadt Consumers Ice Co., Voh's ice house. Part 2 (inset, lower right, own north arrow): The Gregg Co. Ltd., steel and wood industrial cars, Lodi, on the N.Y.S. & W. R.R.; no street junction ('720 ft to Hancock St, see sheet 22'); not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: The Gregg Co. Ltd. car works, Lodi, on the N.Y.S. & W. R.R. (no street junction; only the railroad and works buildings; needs hand-picked control from the works buildings or the N.Y.S. & W. line against Lodi reference data (outside the reference box), step 6b).

sheet-55.description: Sheet 55 covers the eastern edge of Carlstadt and the adjoining part of Woodridge (today Wood-Ridge) at 100 feet to an inch. The dash-dot Carlstadt / Woodridge borough line follows Passaic Avenue in the upper left, Hill Street eastwards, and then Central Avenue down the sheet, with Woodridge to the north and east. On the Carlstadt side Summit Avenue runs along the left edge with Second, Third, Fifth and Sixth Streets crossing, and Passaic Avenue continues south with Seventh, Eighth and Ninth Streets beyond it. In Woodridge, Central Avenue, Union Avenue and Main Avenue run down the sheet, crossed by Charter Oak, Humboldt, Hackensack (on a slant), Washington, Madison, Columbia, Woodridge, Jefferson, Monroe and Railroad, with First Street in the top right. The New Jersey and New York Railroad crosses the bottom of the sheet beside a second street lettered Railroad. Most blocks are laid out in narrow lots with scattered frame dwellings; the large tract east of Passaic Avenue and south of Seventh Street (block 88) and block 22 are nearly empty. Buildings of note are the Woodridge Public School and Fire Dept. Hose Co. No. 1 on Humboldt, St. Paul's Mission Sunday school, a Presbyterian church on Union Avenue, the Carlstadt Bottling Co. on Hackensack Street at Passaic Avenue, a willow basket works on Columbia, the E. B. Elson Mfg. Co. near Union Avenue, the greenhouses of Emil P. Knorr, florist, between Fifth and Sixth Streets, and the Castaldello & Concato embroidery works by the railroad. Stores and a drug store stand along Hackensack Street at Union Avenue.
notes: Central Avenue on the borough line is today Center Street; Hill (Carlstadt side) and Washington (Woodridge side) are today Hill Street; Woodridge is Woodridge Street; Passaic Avenue north of Hackensack Street is today Fritsch Avenue.
Woodridge Public School and Fire Dept. Hose Co. No. 1 on Humboldt Street.
Castaldello & Concato embroidery works beside the New Jersey and New York Railroad.

Scale 100 ft. One part. Carlstadt / Woodridge (Wood-Ridge) from Charter Oak and 2nd St down to the N.J. & N.Y. R.R.: Summit Av (left edge), Passaic Av (Fritsch Avenue north of Hackensack), Central Av (today Center Street, the borough line), Union Av, Main Av; Humboldt, Hackensack, Hill / Washington (today Hill Street), 5th / Madison, 6th / Columbia, 7th / Woodridge, Jefferson, Monroe, Railroad Av. Woodridge Public School, Carlstadt Bottling Co., E. P. Knorr florist.
